question: What do the Vimose runes say?
answer: The sources retrieved do not answer this question. The sources do discuss the Vimose inscriptions, which are earliest datable Elder Futhark runic texts from Scandinavia, but they provide only partial and uncertain interpretations rather than a complete reading of what the inscriptions say [S3].

english.text: In the name of Allah, the Rahman — have mercy upon us, O lord of the heavens; satisfy us by means of your favor; and grant us the essence of it at the end/gift of our days.
english.attribution: Ahmad Al-Jallad, 'A pre-Islamic basmala: reflections on its first epigraphic attestation and its original significance', Jerusalem Studies in Arabic and Islam 52 (2022): 1–28.

english.text: As for this grave/This is a grave, which Ka'b bar Haritat made for Raqash daughter of 'Abd-Manat, his mother. And she died in al-Hijr, year one-hundred-sixty-two, in the month of Tammuz. And may Mare 'Alma [the Lord of the World] curse him who alters this tomb or opens it, save for him whom he has begotten. And may he curse anyone who buries or exhumes anyone else in it.
english.attribution: M. O'Connor's 1986 reading, as reproduced on Wikipedia (JSNab 17), building on Healey's editio.

english.text: harja: likely a personal name or 'comb'/'warrior'. mariha ... makija: possibly 'Mari (the famous one) is the sword of Alla'. awgns: possibly 'son/descendant of Awa'. Several inscriptions remain only partially deciphered.
english.attribution: Kiel Runenprojekt (runenprojekt.uni-kiel.de) interpretive database, as summarized on Wikipedia (Vimose inscriptions).

english.text: Signature on the silver cups: [ΧEIPI]ΣΟΦΟΣ ЄΠΟΙΕΙ ('Cheirisophos made [this]'); engraved owner's name: SILIVS.

...the city where the beautiful vessels, the masterpieces of the Yavanas [Ionians/Greeks-Romans], stir white foam on the Culli [Periyar], a river of the Chera, arriving with gold and departing with pepper—when that Muciri, brimming with prosperity, was besieged by the din of war.
english.attribution: Kulke, Hermann & Rothermund, Dietmar, A History of India (Routledge, 2004), as reproduced on Wikipedia (Muziris).

passages.lang_note: Old Tamil is the weakest language in this pipeline. It matched its own probe at cosine 0.368 where Greek, Literary Chinese and Parthian ran 0.61-0.68, and one machine round trip in three came back in the wrong script. Claims resting on this passage are weaker than claims resting on the Greek.

english.text: Legend on the gold sheet: ANTONINVS AVG PIVS NVRP (or NVAP) XV [slightly corrupted Latin legend]. Diameter 19mm, gold sheet thickness 0.3mm, weight 1.4135g, fineness 916 (22 carat). Formerly Musee Blanchard de la Brosse, Saigon, inv. no. MBB 3460 (unlocated after 1975).
